newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up, then gains more on AGAs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up, then gains more on AGAs.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures, helped by talk of firmer bidweek prices, ended higher Wednesday in a sluggish, post-expiry session, then gained more in overnight trade after a bullish weekly inventory report.

September firmed 4.8 cents to close at $2.161 per million British thermal units, then climbed on ACCESS to $2.18 after the AGA stock data. October settled 3.9 cents higher at $2.155. Others ended mixed, with some 1999s losing ground.

"It (the AGA number) was a bullish number, but the market was going up anyway - there seem to be a lot of people short physical gas," said one Texas-based trader, noting prices during bidweek seemed well supported.
AGA said Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks rose last week by 60 bcf, well below average estimates in the 75-85 bcf range.

Overall stocks are still 162 bcf, or 9.5 percent above year-ago levels, but traders said rising concerns about growing deficits to 1994 and 1995 storage levels, now in the 350-450 bcf range, could help support prices next month.
Below-normal temperatures are blanketing the East and Midwest this week, but normal to slightly above-normal weather was forecast for the weekend.

Chart traders noted September broke minor resistance at the $2.16 double top Wednesday, but most agreed the recent $2.20 high was a more important number. Further selling is likely in the $2.26-2.27 area. Support was seen at $2.08 and then at last week's low of $2.045.

In the cash Wednesday, August Gulf Coast gas firmed a few cents to the mid-to-high teens. August Midcon was up a couple of cents to the $2.07-2.10 area. New York city gate gas for next month was little changed in the low-$2.40s.
The NYMEX Henry Hub 12-month strip rose 1.2 cents to $2.211. NYMEX said 24,293 contracts traded, down sharply from Tuesday's revised tally of 79,386.

On the KCBT, August expired 2.7 cents higher at $2.145, while deferreds ended up by three to 3.5 cents. The September East/West spread widened by 1.5 cents to 9.8 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 1,524 contracts traded, up sharply from Tuesday's total of 699.
